question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding by global health standards?

options.A: The entire first year of life
options.B: The first six months of life
options.D: The first three months of life

explanation: Global health guidelines recommend giving only breast milk for the first six months to ensure the baby grows and develops properly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Why is giving plain water unnecessary for a fully breastfed infant living in a very hot climate?

options.A: Infants cannot swallow water safely during their first few months
options.B: Breast milk is made mostly of water and satisfies the infant's thirst
options.C: Hot weather stops the infant from feeling thirsty
options.D: Water causes immediate stomach pain in newborn babies

explanation: Breast milk contains about eighty-eight percent water, which is more than enough to keep a baby hydrated even in hot weather. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the milk ejection or let-down reflex?
explanation: Oxytocin makes the tiny muscles around the milk glands contract, squeezing the milk out into the ducts for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: What triggers the sharp rise in milk production immediately after childbirth?

options.A: The expulsion of the placenta causing a drop in pregnancy hormones
options.B: The complete emptying of the stomach of the newborn child
options.C: The sudden increase in estrogen levels in the mother's blood
options.D: The infant crying for the very first time in the delivery room

explanation: When the placenta leaves the body, estrogen and progesterone levels drop suddenly, which allows prolactin to start making milk freely. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: What is the name of the thick, yellowish milk produced in the first few days after birth?
explanation: Colostrum is the first milk produced after birth, packed with high concentrations of protective antibodies for the newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: How does Immunoglobulin A (IgA) found in breast milk protect the newborn infant?

options.A: It regulates the baby's body temperature in cold environments
options.B: It coats the intestinal lining to stop germs from entering the body
options.C: It stimulates the baby's pancreas to release digestive enzymes
options.D: It directly increases the infant's red blood cell production

explanation: Secretory IgA forms a protective barrier along the baby's gut, preventing harmful bacteria and viruses from invading. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: How does breastfeeding help a mother's body immediately after delivery?

options.A: It prevents all future menstrual cycles permanently
options.B: It increases total red blood cell volume rapidly
options.C: It repairs perineal tears without surgical intervention
options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions to reduce postpartum bleeding

explanation: Oxytocin released during feeding makes the uterus contract, which helps close blood vessels and lowers the risk of heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h4)

question: What is a long-term health benefit for a woman who practices exclusive breastfeeding?

options.A: Permanent protection from high blood pressure in old age
options.B: Complete immunity against normal aging processes
options.C: Lower risk of developing breast and ovarian cancers
options.D: Elimination of the need for future dental checkups

explanation: Research shows that hormonal changes and reduced lifetime ovulation cycles during breastfeeding lower the risk of certain cancers. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h4)

question: When is the best time to initiate breastfeeding after an uncomplicated delivery?

options.A: Within the first hour of birth
options.B: Once the milk transitions to white
options.D: After the baby receives initial vaccines

explanation: Starting breastfeeding within the first hour takes advantage of the baby's alert state and helps milk production start smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: A nursing student observes a mother struggling to latch her newborn baby. What instruction should the nurse give first?

options.A: Wait until the baby cries loudly to ensure the mouth is open wide enough
options.B: Push the nipple forcefully into the center of the baby's closed mouth
options.C: Bring the baby's wide-open mouth to the breast, not the breast to the baby
options.D: Apply petroleum jelly to the nipple to help the baby slide on easier

explanation: Moving the baby toward the breast ensures a deep latch that includes a large portion of the lower areola, preventing nipple pain. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: What is the most common cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Natural thinning of the skin during pregnancy
options.B: Drinking too little water during the day
options.C: Excessive washing of the breasts with soap

explanation: When a baby only takes the nipple instead of a large part of the areola, friction causes pain and tissue breakdown. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: What is the correct management advice for a mother who develops mastitis in one breast?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent the infection from spreading
options.B: Continue breastfeeding frequently to keep the milk draining out
options.C: Apply ice packs to freeze the infected milk inside the milk ducts
options.D: Stop feeding from the affected side completely until the pain stops

explanation: Frequent milk removal is vital in treating mastitis because letting milk pool in the breast makes the infection worse. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: Why should a nursing mother NEVER use a microwave oven to warm refrigerated breast milk?

options.A: It creates hot spots that burn the baby and destroys immune factors
options.B: It turns the milk into a solid gel that the baby cannot swallow
options.C: It removes all the natural water content from the milk instantly
options.D: It changes the milk color to a dark brown that frightens infants

explanation: Microwaving heats unevenly, creating dangerous hot spots, and the high heat destroys delicate infection-fighting proteins. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h7)

question: What is the rule regarding breast milk that has been frozen and then thawed for a feeding?

options.A: It must be used within twenty-four hours and never refrozen
options.B: It can be placed back in the freezer for up to one month safely
options.C: It can sit safely at room temperature for up to two full days
options.D: It must be boiled on a stove before giving it to the infant

explanation: Once thawed, bacteria can multiply quickly in breast milk, so it must be used promptly and discarded if left over. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h7)

question: What is the primary reason mothers often give early formula supplementation that nurses should proactively address?

options.A: A medical dislike for the taste of human breast milk
options.B: Anxiety and worry about having insufficient milk supply
options.C: Physical inability to hold a bottle during the day
options.D: Advice from pediatricians to stop feeding at night

explanation: Many mothers worry their milk is not enough when babies cluster-feed, so proactive reassurance and education prevent unnecessary formula use. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct responsibility of the nurse supporting a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Providing reassurance and guidance on managing sore nipples
options.B: Deciding whether the family should buy formula or breast pumps
options.C: Assisting with early skin-to-skin contact in the delivery room
options.D: Teaching proper latching and positioning techniques

explanation: Nurses educate and support feeding choices and techniques, but families make their own purchasing and feeding decisions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h8)
